title: Root Account Usage

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.2 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.2 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" userIdentity.type="Root"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.2_root_account_usage_2"
| sort -_time
description: The AWS root account has unrestricted access and should never be used for daily operations. Any root activity is a critical security event.
value: Detecting root account usage early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: CloudTrail must be enabled in all regions. Create a critical real-time alert on any event where `userIdentity.type=Root`. Exclude expected events (e.g., automated billing).
visualization: Events list (critical alert), Single value (root events last 30d), Timeline.
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
  where match(Authentication.user, "(?i)arn:aws:iam::[0-9]+:root|\\bRoot\\b")
  by Authentication.src Authentication.action Authentication.app span=1h
| sort -count
dataModelAcceleration: Authentication: map `aws:cloudtrail` `userIdentity` to CIM, then enable Authentication acceleration. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: Initial account setup, rare billing or support cases your policy still routes through root; documented break-glass; MFA and payment instrument changes in small businesses.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
CloudTrail must be enabled in all regions. Create a critical real-time alert on any event where `userIdentity.type=Root`. Exclude expected events (e.g., automated billing).
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" userIdentity.type="Root"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.2_root_account_usage_2"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect root account usage. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_2_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Events list (critical alert), Single value (root events last 30d), Timeline..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of root account usage so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
